candidates.original_title: Different tests, different answers: The stability of teacher value-added estimates across outcome measures
candidates.description: Teacher VAM scores from models using spring-to-spring test score changes are essentially orthogonal (correlation of -.10) to those same teachers' VAM scores from a model using fall-to-fall test score changes
candidates.citation_sentence: Results from the current study generally align with findings from a similar analysis embedded in Papay (2011) and hold up against the additional robustness checks we are able to bring to bear.

candidates.original_title: Different Tests, Different Answers: The Stability of Teacher Value-Added Estimates Across Outcome Measures
candidates.description: Teacher value-added scores based on fall-to-fall and spring-to-spring test-score timing have a weak correlation, producing substantially different rankings of teacher effectiveness.
candidates.citation_sentence: In one such study, Papay (2011) briefly shows that teacher VAM scores from models using the most common pre/post testing timeframe-that is, based on changes in test scores from last spring to current spring-are essentially orthogonal (correlation of -.10) to those same teachers' VAM scores from a model using test score changes from current fall to next fall.
candidates.notes: The paper reports that its findings generally align with Papay (2011), documenting very low correlations between fall-to-fall and spring-to-spring teacher VAM scores in both ELA and math.
